item.title: Adolescent Mental Health Patients Report Mixed Outcomes From Online Health Portals - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: Adolescents' experiences using electronic patient portals in specialized mental health care
  • Article Title: Experiences of using patient portals as adolescents in mental health care – a qualitative study
  • Experiences of using patient portals as adolescents in mental health care – a qualitative study. BMC Digital Health, 4(1), Article 34. https://doi.org/10.1186/s44247-026-00269-6

본문

Adolescents receiving specialist mental health care report both significant empowering benefits and marked psychological challenges when accessing their electronic health records through digital patient portals, according to a qualitative investigation conducted in Norway. The study evaluated how young patients interact with electronic portal services, revealing that direct access to clinical records can encourage autonomy and assist treatment management, while simultaneously exposing individuals to unexpected distress, re-traumatization, and strained therapeutic relationships. Published in BMC Digital Health by Martine Stecher Hornum, Aslak Steinsbekk, and Torunn Hatlen Nøst, the research addresses an established knowledge gap regarding how adolescents specifically navigate online medical records during mental health treatment.

As digital health infrastructure expands globally, adolescents receiving mental health services are increasingly encouraged to take greater responsibility for managing their ongoing care. Patient portals offer digital gateways that allow individuals to review their electronic health records, monitor diagnostic and consultation notes, track scheduled consultations, and communicate directly with their medical providers. While prior research in adult psychiatric populations and pediatric somatic care indicated that electronic access could bolster engagement, transparent communication, and self-efficacy, limited empirical attention had focused on adolescents undergoing psychiatric interventions. Clinicians had historically raised concerns regarding patient comprehension, confidentiality boundaries between adolescents and their guardians, and the emotional impact of reading unmediated clinical evaluations.

To explore these complex dynamics, researchers designed a qualitative study involving individual semi-structured interviews with 17 individuals who had direct experience using patient portals while receiving care in child and adolescent specialist mental health services in Norway. Participants ranged from 16 to 27 years of age at the time of data collection, with a mean age of 20, and more than 80 percent of the sample identified as female. Approximately half of the participants were attending high school when interviewed. Although the upper age limit extended to 27 to allow reflective evaluation of adolescent experiences, the study strictly included individuals who had interacted with portals during their adolescent psychiatric treatment, ensuring retrospective depth alongside proximate experience.

item.title: Digital Health Educator Transition Entails Professional Identity Shifts Beyond Technical Skills - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: Qualitative analysis of health professions educators transitioning to digital education using Schlossberg's transition theory
  • Article Title: Navigating the transition to digital health professions education: a qualitative study of faculty development through the lens of Schlossberg’s transition theory
  • Navigating the transition to digital health professions education: a qualitative study of faculty development through the lens of Schlossberg’s transition theory. BMC Medical Education, 26(1), Article 1858. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-10761-2

본문

Transitioning into digital health professions education represents a complex evolution that extends far beyond acquiring technical competencies, according to a qualitative investigation published in BMC Medical Education. The study demonstrates that becoming a digital health professions educator entails a fundamental transformation of professional identity, shaped by an ongoing interplay of personal and professional characteristics, the level of digital integration within educational environments, institutional and peer support, and the deliberate strategies educators employ to acquire and apply new pedagogical skills. Investigating participants enrolled in a certified faculty development programme, researchers found that educators navigate the process of redefining their professional roles within digital learning spaces through a multifaceted adjustment process rather than a simple technical update.

Health professions educators must often manage multiple demanding roles simultaneously as clinicians, researchers, and teachers, all while adapting to the broader transition to digital education. Although faculty development initiatives are routinely designed to support educators in adapting to this rapidly changing educational landscape, researchers noted that there has remained a limited understanding of how professionals actually navigate this complex transition. To address this empirical gap, the qualitative study explored how experienced health professions educators navigate the process of redefining their roles within digital learning environments through their active participation in a one-year certified digital faculty development programme.

The research was conducted with participants enrolled in the Digital Health Professions Educator programme, designated as the DHPE programme, at Charité–Universitätsmedizin Berlin. This specialized curriculum was designed as a certified, 200-hour course tailored specifically for experienced educators from diverse healthcare disciplines seeking to advance their instructional capabilities. To capture detailed qualitative data regarding the participants’ lived transition experiences, the research team conducted two focus group discussions alongside seven semi-structured interviews. In total, fifteen experienced health professions educators took part in the investigation, representing an overall response rate of 71 percent. All gathered discussions and interview dialogues were transcribed to facilitate rigorous textual evaluation across the full range of participant accounts.

item.title: Personal Health Data Spaces Require Responsive Implementation to Achieve True Care Continuity - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: Implementation frameworks and continuous care evaluation for personal health data spaces
  • Article Title: From interoperable data to continuous care: a responsive implementation approach to personal health data spaces
  • From interoperable data to continuous care: a responsive implementation approach to personal health data spaces. Frontiers in Medicine, 13, Article 1966291. https://doi.org/10.3389/fmed.2026.1966291

본문

Personal health data spaces cannot successfully transform fragmented medical care into continuous, coordinated treatment through technical interoperability alone, according to an analytical opinion paper published in Frontiers in Medicine by implementation researcher Bo Kim. Personal health data spaces promise to grant individuals meaningful, longitudinal control over their health information while enabling heterogeneous clinical records, patient-reported metrics, and wearable data to move across disparate settings of care without requiring burdensome reconstructions at every clinical transition. However, Kim emphasizes that mere technical availability does not equate to genuine care continuity. A digital architecture can be technically interoperable, robustly secured, and formally patient-controlled while still remaining frustratingly difficult to navigate, weakly integrated into daily clinical workflows, or inaccessible to marginalized populations. The fundamental challenge facing modern digital health initiatives is therefore not simply constructing data architectures, but implementing them deliberately so that shared medical data actually foster actionable clinical relationships and reliable care coordination across healthcare systems.

Synthesizing contributions from a dedicated Frontiers Research Topic, the analysis illustrates how technical capabilities and behavioral realities must converge within personal health data spaces. One foundational study by Ambalavanan and colleagues proposes a layered, modular, ontology-driven front-end architecture that links user experience, system security, data governance, semantic interoperability, analytics, and infrastructure scalability. In a complementary investigation, Lin and colleagues detail a blockchain-supported dynamic consent framework designed to allow participants to trace, modify, and revoke data permissions over time rather than treating consent as an inflexible, one-time transaction. Meanwhile, an empirical cross-sectional study by Ruan and colleagues involving patients at elevated risk of stroke demonstrates that proactive health behaviors are strongly associated with health literacy, self-efficacy, available social support, and socioeconomic circumstances. When evaluated collectively, these studies demonstrate that technically capable digital health platforms will only generate continuous care if embedded within an implementation system that renders participation understandable, practically supported, actionable, and continually revisable.

item.title: Randomised Trial Protocol Outlines Smartphone Glucose Monitoring in Gestational Diabetes - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Because this document details an established study protocol rather than the completed trial, its published scope outlines the prospective trial design without reporting clinical results, intervention efficacy, or patient health outcomes.
  • Article Title: Smartphone and internet-based glucose management system for gestational diabetes: study protocol for a randomised controlled trial (M♡THer study)
  • Smartphone and internet-based glucose management system for gestational diabetes: study protocol for a randomised controlled trial (M♡THer study).

본문

Researchers have published the protocol for a randomised controlled trial evaluating a smartphone and internet-based blood glucose management platform for gestational diabetes. Known as the M♡THer study, the clinical trial is designed to determine whether remote digital monitoring can serve as an effective alternative to conventional clinic-based care for pregnant women diagnosed with the condition.

Gestational diabetes is defined as carbohydrate intolerance resulting in hyperglycaemia of variable severity, with onset or first recognition during pregnancy. The metabolic disorder is associated with elevated clinical risks for both mother and fetus, while also imposing a substantial burden on pregnant women and healthcare services. Standard care currently relies on frequent ambulatory in-clinic visits to assess glycemic control.

While smartphone and internet-based systems offer an alternative model of care through remote physiological monitoring, substantial evidence evaluating mobile health interventions in gestational diabetes remains lacking. The newly outlined trial aims to provide high-quality evidence concerning the clinical effectiveness, safety, and health service impact of a digitally enabled care pathway.

The study is structured as a pragmatic, unblinded, single-centre, parallel-group, non-inferiority randomised controlled trial with a 1:1 allocation ratio. Participants will be assigned to either remote blood glucose monitoring using the M♡THer digital platform or standard clinic-based monitoring throughout their pregnancy.

Under the digital intervention, participants track capillary blood glucose levels at home and transmit readings in near real time to healthcare providers using a validated Bluetooth-enabled glucometer and mobile application. The trial’s primary outcome is the proportion of blood glucose readings that fall within the targeted therapeutic range during pregnancy.

Secondary outcomes include additional glycaemic measures, maternal and neonatal clinical outcomes, healthcare utilisation, and patient satisfaction ratings. The trial was prospectively registered in May 2025 with the Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry under registration identifier ACTRN12625000547448, with researchers noting that findings could inform future diabetes management models in rural and remote settings.

Because this document details an established study protocol rather than the completed trial, its published scope outlines the prospective trial design without reporting clinical results, intervention efficacy, or patient health outcomes.

item.title: Electronic Record Linkage Cuts Clinician Social Care Time by Seventy Percent - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: Evaluation of digital interoperability between clinical electronic patient records and social prescribing systems in secondary mental health services
  • Article Title: Interoperability between clinical electronic patient record and social prescribing systems: The Life Rooms service evaluation
  • Interoperability between clinical electronic patient record and social prescribing systems: The Life Rooms service evaluation. BMC Digital Health, 4(1), Article 35. https://doi.org/10.1186/s44247-026-00265-w

본문

A service evaluation conducted within the National Health Service in England has demonstrated that establishing digital interoperability between a clinical electronic patient record system and a dedicated social prescribing platform significantly streamlined care pathways while reducing the time secondary mental health clinicians spent addressing non-clinical concerns. The evaluation, published in BMC Digital Health, investigated the operational deployment of linked digital infrastructure across Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust, which became the first NHS trust in the United Kingdom to connect its primary electronic patient record software, Access Rio, with the specialized social prescribing platform Access Elemental. Operating through The Life Rooms, an NHS community-facing service that targets the wider social determinants of health, the integration allowed secondary mental health professionals to make direct, automated electronic referrals to non-clinical link workers, known locally as Pathways Advisors. Clinicians who completed an evaluation survey following the implementation reported a seventy percent reduction in the average time required to handle practical social problems during clinical appointments, dropping from twenty-seven minutes down to eight minutes per session. Simultaneously, ninety-seven point two percent of surveyed clinicians reported increased personal confidence in managing their patients’ non-medical needs, while more than ninety-two percent of surveyed service users reported tangible improvements in their mental wellbeing following their engagement with the social prescribing team.

item.title: Co-Creation Study Identifies Feasible Strategies for Integrating Cancer Screening Information - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: Qualitative evaluation of digital portals and integrated information strategies for population-based cancer screening
  • Article Title: Enhancing the accessibility of population-based cancer screening: insights from co-creation on a screening portal and a combined screening programme
  • Enhancing the accessibility of population-based cancer screening: insights from co-creation on a screening portal and a combined screening programme. Frontiers in Digital Health, 8, Article 1947552. https://doi.org/10.3389/fdgth.2026.1947552

본문

A qualitative co-creation study conducted by researchers in the Netherlands has identified that integrating health communication across national cancer screening programmes represents a feasible and highly valued approach to improving participation, whereas combining multiple physical screening procedures into a single appointment presents substantial logistical and professional obstacles. Published in Frontiers in Digital Health, the investigation evaluated two complementary strategies aimed at reversing recent declines in population-based cancer screening attendance: developing a personalised digital screening portal and evaluating the operational feasibility of combining breast, cervical, and colorectal cancer screening. By pairing screening invitees directly with domain experts in human factors engineering and national screening management, the research team gathered qualitative evidence on how digital customisation and organisational coordination could reduce fragmentation and support informed decision-making without disrupting healthcare delivery systems.

Organised population-based screening programmes play a pivotal role in national cancer control strategies by detecting early-stage malignancies, which significantly reduces cancer-related morbidity and mortality. Within the Dutch healthcare framework, three primary programmes target specific general population cohorts: colorectal cancer screening for men and women aged 55 to 75 administered biennially via home-based faecal immunochemical tests; breast cancer screening for women aged 50 to 75 conducted biennially through mammography units; and cervical cancer screening for women aged 30 to 60 administered every five or ten years via human papillomavirus testing. Despite established clinical benefits, recent administrative figures demonstrate declining uptake across all three tracks. In 2025, participation rates in the Netherlands reached 67 percent for colorectal screening, 70 percent for breast screening, and 50 percent for cervical screening. Moreover, a 2022 cross-sectional cohort analysis revealed that among Dutch women aged 55, only 54 percent participated in all three programmes, while 22 percent completed two, 12 percent completed one, and 12 percent abstained entirely, indicating substantial drop-off across overlapping screening invitations.

item.description:
요약

  • DHP 2026 성료…의료AI 기업 해외 매출 성과·글로벌 진출 전략 공유
  • 디지털 헬스케어 파트너스(DHP)가 11월 11일과 12일 서울 플렌티 컨벤션에서 개최한 ‘DHP 2026: Breakout to the Globe’를 마쳤다.
  • 발표에 따르면 루닛의 해외 매출 비중은 92%, 에어스메디컬은 85%, 쓰리빌리언은 67%, 코어라인소프트는 62%다.

본문

DHP 2026 성료…의료AI 기업 해외 매출 성과·글로벌 진출 전략 공유

디지털 헬스케어 파트너스(DHP)가 11월 11일과 12일 서울 플렌티 컨벤션에서 개최한 ‘DHP 2026: Breakout to the Globe’를 마쳤다. 올해 처음 이틀 일정으로 열린 행사에는 1,300여 명이 참석했으며, 글로벌 진출 주역 37명이 전략과 경험을 공유했다.

DHP는 국내 의료기기 시장이 11조9,000억원 규모지만 세계 시장에서 차지하는 비중은 1.5%라며 글로벌 진출의 필요성을 강조했다. 발표에 따르면 루닛의 해외 매출 비중은 92%, 에어스메디컬은 85%, 쓰리빌리언은 67%, 코어라인소프트는 62%다.

첫날 키노트에는 김경훈 OpenAI 코리아 총괄 대표와 최준일 삼성헬스 상무가 나섰다. 김 대표는 환자의 건강기록 이해를 돕는 ‘ChatGPT 헬스’와 에픽 연동 진료 준비 기능, 생명과학 연구용 ‘GPT-Rosalind’를 소개했다. 최 상무는 헬스케어 밸류체인 개선과 플랫폼 생태계, 정밀의료를 위한 디지털 헬스 인프라 전략을 발표했다.

서준범 국가인공지능전략위원회 기본의료TF 팀장은 AI 기본의료 전략을 설명했다. 이어 루닛, 씨어스, 쓰리빌리언, 코어라인소프트 대표가 규제 대응과 현지화, 데이터 활용, 해외 검진사업 경험을 공유했다. 코어라인소프트는 폐암검진 솔루션 ‘AVIEW’가 19개국에서 300만건 이상의 분석 실적을 쌓았다고 밝혔다.

의료 시스템을 해외에 구축한 사례도 소개됐다. 에이치플러스 양지병원은 2024년 12월 베트남 하노이에 문을 연 에이치플러스 국제의료센터를 한국 디지털 헬스케어 기업의 실증 거점으로 활용하겠다고 밝혔다. 헬스커넥트는 해외 병원에 환자관리 운영체계를 먼저 이식한 뒤 한국 솔루션을 결합하는 ‘거점 단위 수출’ 모델을 제시했다. 케이닥은 인도네시아 발리국제병원에 한국형 소화기센터를 열고 10년간 수탁 운영을 맡은 사례를 발표했다.

둘째 날에는 에어스메디컬과 강남언니가 해외 시장에서 매출을 만든 경험을 공유했다. 에어스메디컬은 MRI 촬영 시간을 절반으로 줄이는 AI로 50개 이상 국가의 1,800개 병원에 진출했다고 밝혔다. 이어진 다섯 개 트랙에서는 스타트업 16곳이 미국, 일본, 동남아 시장에서 거둔 성과와 시행착오를 발표했다.

미국에서는 픽스업 헬스가 31개 병원에서 AI 원격 모니터링과 보험청구 자동화의 보험 상환 성과를 냈고, 위트젠은 생성형 AI ‘가상세포’ 기술로 현지 암센터와 협력하고 있다고 소개했다. 일본에서는 무니스가 출시 12개월 만에 일본 앱스토어 헬스케어·피트니스 부문 1위에 올랐고, 휴레이 헬스케어는 현지 기업 인수와 유통망을 통해 일본 클리닉 850여 곳을 확보했다고 밝혔다. 티알이는 베트남 130개 병원에 제품을 공급하고 아스트라제네카와 공동 마케팅을 시작한 사례를 공유했다.

행사장에는 24개 후원사의 전시 부스가 마련됐다. DHP는 현재 국내외 60여 개 디지털 헬스케어 스타트업에 투자하고 15개 헬스케어 펀드를 운용하고 있으며, 내년 DHP 2027을 개최할 계획이라고 밝혔다.

item.title: Clinicians Prefer Layered Visualizations and Contextual Logs for Wearable Health Data - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: Clinician preferences for wearable health data visualization and behavioral context integration
  • Article Title: Exploring clinician preferences for visualizing wearable health data: insights from UK anesthesiologists and Mexican general practitioners
  • Exploring clinician preferences for visualizing wearable health data: insights from UK anesthesiologists and Mexican general practitioners. Frontiers in Digital Health, 8, Article 1909166. https://doi.org/10.3389/fdgth.2026.1909166

본문

Practicing clinicians evaluating prototype wearable monitoring interfaces expressed a decisive preference for hierarchical data visualizations that open with broad trend summaries before supporting drill-down inspection into finer temporal intervals, according to a qualitative study published in Frontiers in Digital Health. Investigating how complex, multimodal wearable outputs can be translated into actionable clinical insights, researchers assessed feedback from acute care anesthesiologists in the United Kingdom and primary care general practitioners in Mexico. Across both clinical cohorts, participants indicated that continuous physiological streams alone are frequently insufficient for sound clinical interpretation without concurrent contextual and behavioral data, such as records of sleep quality, emotional stress, food intake, and physical exertion.

Wearable Health Monitoring Systems continuously capture physiological, behavioral, and environmental parameters in real-world settings, offering longitudinal visibility into health status that episodic hospital measurements cannot provide. Nevertheless, the volume and complexity of multi-source, multi-rate data streams create substantial interpretation bottlenecks for healthcare practitioners. Existing clinical visualization systems often fail to match the cognitive demands of medical workflows, occasionally relying on inappropriate visual encodings, limited interactivity, or rigid presentation formats that obscure subtle physiological changes. To identify design strategies capable of bridging this information gap, researchers David Infante Sanchez and Aikaterini Bourazeri investigated how specific graphical representations interact with clinical tasks across distinct healthcare environments.

To generate realistic continuous data for clinician evaluation, the research team designed PatientSense, a custom wearable health monitoring prototype built from off-the-shelf electronic components and open-source software tools centered on a Feather M0 processor board. The hardware configuration incorporated two dedicated devices: one tailored for daytime monitoring and another configured for nocturnal sleep tracking, complete with an external environmental sensing module. During the daytime, the system captured pulse rate at 500 Hz using an optical sensor, electrodermal activity at 41.6 Hz through silver-silver chloride electrodes, body temperature at 0.33 Hz, physical activity and metabolic equivalent of task values using a three-axis accelerometer, and ambient light and temperature. During sleep, it recorded pulse rate, body temperature, electrooculography, actigraphy, ambient sound via an electret microphone, and environmental lighting.

item.title: Moving healthcare AI from pilot to practice - Fierce Healthcare
item.description:
요약

  • Many of us have already experienced promising AI pilots. The question I hear most now is how to move from small experiments to enterprise-wide deployment.
  • In my conversations about AI with providers and payers, I hear genuine excitement balanced by healthy pragmatism. None of us are ready for an AI doctor giving a diagnosis but documentation, phone calls, referrals, and back-office work?
  • - An agent can take a request in plain language, use connectors to reach into different systems of record, apply skills to reason through the context, and propose next steps for a person to approve.

본문

Whether we’re physicians, nurses, care managers, or the people who keep coverage and claims moving, most of us entered healthcare to help people. This responsibility gives us an extraordinary sense of purpose, but also makes us cautious about new technology. Yet for the first time in my career, I see healthcare leaning in, because AI is exceptionally good at the repetitive work that sits between us and the patients we serve.

Many of us have already experienced promising AI pilots. The question I hear most now is how to move from small experiments to enterprise-wide deployment.

We’ve built healthcare technology one portal and system of record at a time. In a large health system, people navigate at least 10 to 20 systems, each with its own login and dataset for each patient. For every hour physicians spend with patients, they spend nearly two more on EHR and desk work, plus one to two hours of “pajama time.” We're short on clinicians, and we keep asking them to do paperwork instead of practicing at the top of their license.

When I grew up in India, the doctor near my home knew me personally from handwritten notes. Today I’m an EHR in a big system that holds far more data about me, yet still doesn’t know me the way that doctor did. Healthcare today is data rich but intelligence poor. AI can help us put the right data in front of the right person, in the right context, at the right time.

In my conversations about AI with providers and payers, I hear genuine excitement balanced by healthy pragmatism. None of us are ready for an AI doctor giving a diagnosis but documentation, phone calls, referrals, and back-office work? I see very little resistance to getting time back.

Introducing Gemini for healthcare

Gemini for healthcare connects data, intelligence, and action, so healthcare professionals can spend less time as human integrators and more time caring for people. Instead of simply putting a chatbot in front of clinicians or benefits specialists, it brings AI into healthcare systems and workflows through three capabilities: connectors, skills, and agents.

- Connectors bring the context via authorized access to EHRs such as Epic, Oracle Cerner, and Meditech, and to sources such as PubMed, CMS coverage data, and the NPI registry.

- A skill is a reusable way to instruct an agent to do a task, such as preparing a prior authorization or synthesizing a 100-page medical record without missing anything pertinent. We’re launching with five, developed in close partnership with customers.

- An agent can take a request in plain language, use connectors to reach into different systems of record, apply skills to reason through the context, and propose next steps for a person to approve.

item.title: The new digital frontier for healthcare’s most resilient communication tool: The fax - wyomingnewsnow.tv
item.description:
요약

  • This is the paradox inside the American medical record in 2026. The information is usually there. It often even counts as available. But available and usable are not the same, and the gap between them can be where a surprising share of a patient's history disappears.
  • The Records That Arrive but Never Become Readable
  • And it did not come back evenly. Among hospitals that belong to a larger health system, 53% routinely share records electronically across all the major settings they exchange with. Among independent hospitals, the kind that fill rural counties and small towns, that figure is 22%.

본문

The electronic health record was supposed to end the era of lost documentation. Hospitals adopted digital systems by the thousands, and the federal government spent more than a decade pushing patient records online. Yet fax remains one of the most resilient communication channels in American healthcare, and for good reason: It reaches the small and rural facilities that other systems might not have fully connected. Even as digital exchange expands, hospital reliance on secure fax transmission persists.

The real problem, however, was the format. Somewhere this afternoon, a staff member at a small hospital is working through a stack of inbound documents, retyping medication lists and referral notes into the very system meant to hold them. Nothing was lost. Everything arrived. It simply arrived as flat images that a computer cannot read.

This is the paradox inside the American medical record in 2026. The information is usually there. It often even counts as available. But available and usable are not the same, and the gap between them can be where a surprising share of a patient's history disappears.

Getting a record from one place to another is one job. Making it usable once it arrives is another. Legacy paper-based workflows solved the first and ignored the second. Digital cloud fax works on both fronts: It uses a channel hospitals already run, paired with intelligent data extraction that turns scanned pages and free-text notes into structured, usable data.

Digital cloud fax provider eFax analyzed federal interoperability data and industry document-volume estimates to map this disconnect inside America's medical records. What the numbers describe is a system that receives information but cannot fully use it, on a scale most patients never see, and a clear path to finally surfacing it.

The Records That Arrive but Never Become Readable

In 2023, 71% of hospitals had routine access to patient information from outside sources at the point of care. Only 42% said their clinicians often used it.

Access means the document showed up. Use means a person could actually pull the medical detail out of it in the moment a decision had to be made. Roughly three in four hospitals also fold what they receive directly into their own records, while about a quarter still retype it by hand.

The reason so much arrives without becoming readable lies in the shape of the information itself. A clinical note, a scanned discharge summary, a faxed referral: to a person, these are full of meaning. To the software meant to file them, they are a flat image or a wall of free text that it can’t process.

At the INVEST DIgital Health conference in Dallas, the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H) offered a glimpse of the kind of technology it’s funding. MedCity News Reporter Marissa Plescia did a series of video interviews with a selection of companies in ARPA-H’s portfolio that exhibited in the Innovation Showcase.

Chief Commercial Officer Dan Rodenhaver discussed how NIRSense‘s biosensor development has created the ability to treat more advanced disease states at home. The challenge is the industry requires new data inputs rather than advanced applications of existing data. In an interview, Rodenhaver told Marissa Plescia that advances in optical sensing technology means that it can collect data one would previously need a blood test to obtain. Funded by the Department of Defense, the business develops prototypes with the goal of finding strategic partners who can commercialize its technology.

Sibel Health has created a couple of flexible, wireless, wearable vital sign monitors designed to capture vital sign information to identify early signs of patient deterioration. The company’s two wearables include a pulse oximeter and a chest monitor to capture blood oxygen and heart data as well as other patient information. In an interview, Director of Customer Success and Clinical Implementation Beth Schreiber explained how the wearables work and how they can help clinicians.

item.title: African health leaders adopt Nairobi Action Agenda to turn health data into better healthcare - WHO | Regional Office for Africa
item.description:
요약

  • The commitments respond to findings from two WHO reports launched during the forum.
  • The Maturity and Functionality of Health Information System in the WHO African Region, based on an assessment of 40 countries, found an overall maturity score of 59 out of 100, highlighting significant gaps in financing, governance and analytical capacity.
  • Country experiences presented during the forum, including initiatives from Ethiopia, Rwanda, Kenya and Egypt, demonstrated how countries are using digital technologies and stronger information systems to improve health planning and services.

본문

Nairobi, 12 November 2026, Government representatives and health partners meeting in Nairobi have adopted a new action agenda to strengthen health information systems and ensure that reliable health data are used to improve healthcare services, prevent avoidable deaths and reach communities most in need.

The Nairobi Health Data Action Agenda, adopted at the conclusion of the First Africa Health Data Forum, sets out eight priorities to help countries move beyond collecting and reporting health information towards using it to guide policies, direct investments and improve people's health.

“The Nairobi Health Data Action Agenda must translate countries’ priorities into practical investments that can be financed, implemented and measured. Ultimately, every investment in health information must make a difference in people's lives, through better decisions, stronger health services and improved health outcomes” said Dr Abdurahmane Diallo, Director of Programme Management, WHO Regional Office for Africa.

Convened by the World Health Organization (WHO) in collaboration with partners, the three-day forum brought together Ministers of Health, senior government officials, WHO leadership and development partners to take stock of progress, address persistent gaps in health information systems and agree on practical actions.

Despite significant progress that countries are making in digital health reporting and data collection, many countries continue to face fragmented information systems, inadequate financing, shortages of skilled professionals and limited capacity to translate available information into effective decisions.

Under the Nairobi Action Agenda, countries committed to strengthening national leadership, increasing sustainable domestic financing, improving the quality of health information and connecting fragmented data systems. The Agenda also prioritizes investment in skilled professionals, responsible use of digital health and artificial intelligence, and the routine use of evidence in healthcare planning and resource allocation.

The commitments respond to findings from two WHO reports launched during the forum.

The Maturity and Functionality of Health Information System in the WHO African Region, based on an assessment of 40 countries, found an overall maturity score of 59 out of 100, highlighting significant gaps in financing, governance and analytical capacity.

The second report “Health Data Systems and Capacity in Africa”, based on the SCORE 2025 assessment of 52 countries, found that while countries have made progress in monitoring health-system performance, none had reached the highest level of sustainable capacity for using data and evidence effectively in policy and action.

Country experiences presented during the forum, including initiatives from Ethiopia, Rwanda, Kenya and Egypt, demonstrated how countries are using digital technologies and stronger information systems to improve health planning and services.
